v.why: Edge 1 feeds node 2, whose only exit edge 5 is removed, so the edit is dead.
Edge 4 leaves node 1, which gets no input when edge 0 is none, so the edge is disconnected.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, which cannot reach the output when edge 5 is none.
Edge 2 leaves node 1, which has no input when edge 0 is none, so the edge is dead.
Removing edge 1 costs little when node 2 cannot reach the output.
Removing edge 4 costs little when node 1 receives no input.
Removing edge 2 costs little when node 2's output edge is already none.
Removing edge 2 costs little when node 1 is already disconnected from the input.
Edge 4 is disconnected when edge 0 is none, so setting it to skip_connect loses the usual gain.
Adding a conv to a missing direct edge gives a large capacity gain, more than replacing an existing op.
